name: kilobat
description: Diagnose slow or flaky internet on a Mac: per-app traffic, Wi-Fi signal, latency, DNS and speed tests.
long_description: Kilobat measures your Mac's network so Claude can explain why the internet is slow: Wi-Fi signal and noise, router and internet latency, jitter, packet loss, DNS, captive portals, nearby networks, per-app traffic, usage history and a data-capped speed test against Cloudflare. It also keeps the Mac awake for long runs, finds the layer that stops one host, shows each app's bandwidth over time and what it declares it connects to, and answers apps waiting for approval. Diagnostic tools are read-only. Tools that change a profile, a rule, the new-app mode, an approval or DNS are annotated as destructive so Claude asks first. Network history is stored locally; requested MCP results are shared with the connected AI client under its data policies. Blocking requires the Kilobat app with its network filter enabled. macOS 14 or later.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Per-app network traffic on this Mac right now: connection, network kind (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Cellular), whether it is metered (hotspot), active profile, total download/upload bytes per second, session bytes, and each app's rates and saved allow/block rule. Samples for 2–8 seconds. Same JSON as `kilobat status --json`.

tools.name: diagnose_network
tools.description: Checks Wi-Fi signal, the local router, internet latency, DNS and captive portals in a few seconds. Returns `health` (good, degraded, poor, unknown), plain-language `advice`, `signalScore` (0–100), `signalNoiseRatio` (dB), `routerLatencyMs`, `internetLatencyMs`, `internetJitterMs` and raw `measurements`: radio RSSI/noise/channel/band, router and internet ping average, jitter and loss, DNS lookup milliseconds, resolvers and captivePortal. Start here for slow or flaky internet. Same JSON as `kilobat diagnose --json`.

tools.name: scan_wifi
tools.description: Lists nearby Wi-Fi networks with SSID, RSSI and noise (dBm), channel, band and channel width, to spot crowded channels or a stronger access point. Names come from the running Kilobat app, which has Location permission; without it SSIDs read "Hidden network". An empty list means scanning is unavailable. Same JSON as `kilobat scan --json`.

tools.name: run_speedtest
tools.description: Measures download and upload Mbps against Cloudflare plus latency under load (`bufferbloat`: Low, Moderate, High or Inconclusive; `addedLatencyMs`). Also returns `voiceCalls`, `videoCalls` and `streaming` verdicts (the highest quality the bandwidth supports, and whether it may stutter) and `callWarnings` explaining any caution. Takes up to about 30 seconds and transfers up to `budget_mb` of data (80 MB by default). On a metered or hotspot connection, get the user's confirmation first and pass a small budget such as 10. `measurements` also records `streams`, `server` (the Cloudflare data center) and `context` (interface, connection kind, VPN, Wi-Fi band, channel, signal and link rate, and `otherBytes` this Mac moved during the test), and `method` says how it measured. One connection (the default) reads lower than Ookla, fast.com or networkQuality on fast or distant links because those open several; pass `parallel` for four connections at once when the user compares with such a site. Same JSON as `kilobat speedtest --json`.

tools.name: get_usage_report
tools.description: Data used on this Mac over the last `days` (7 by default): download and upload totals, per-day totals and the top 10 apps by bytes. History is recorded while the Kilobat app runs and never leaves the Mac. Same JSON as `kilobat report --summary --json --days N`.

tools.name: compare_usage
tools.description: Sets a router's, ISP's or carrier's data figure beside what Kilobat recorded on this Mac for the same period, networks and direction. Pass `total` and its `unit` exactly as the router or provider shows them (GB is decimal, GiB binary; many providers write GB for either), `direction` (both, download or upload) and the period: `from` and `to` (2026-10-01, 2026-10-01 18:00 or ISO 8601 with an offset; a date-only `to` includes that day; ask the user for the provider's time zone when it matters) or a `period` preset. `network` limits it to one network by name or key from list_networks. Returns Kilobat's `kilobatBytes` and `kilobatAmount` in the same unit, `downloadBytes`, `uploadBytes`, `differenceBytes` (the figure minus Kilobat), `alternateBytes` (the figure read in the other unit system), `localBytes` (local network and AirDrop, not counted), `unattributedBytes` (packet headers and the like, counted), `otherNetworkBytes`, `periodHours`, `recordedHours`, `coverage`, `gaps` (`start`, `end`, `hours`, `reason`: asleep, notRecorded, otherNetwork, beforeHistory or notYet), `networks`, `topApps`, a `summary` and `reasons`, the likely causes of the difference in plain English, most likely first. Kilobat sees only this Mac and only while it runs, so a router or provider total is usually higher; relay the reasons and never conclude that the provider, the router or Kilobat is wrong, or that the difference proves malware or a billing error. Same JSON as `kilobat report compare --json`.

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: Rules for the active profile, or for `profile` if given: the profile name, whether it is `active`, whether unknown apps are allowed by default, saved allow/block rules by bundle ID or process:<name>, unexpired temporary rules, the data `budget` (limit, `cycle`, `alerts`, `usedBytes` this cycle and when it `resets`) and app `quotas` with their use. Same JSON as `kilobat rules --json [--profile name]`.

tools.name: set_profile
tools.description: Selects a profile. travel allows only essential apps to save mobile or hotspot data, work pauses distractions, unrestricted allows every app. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling. Blocking takes effect only while the Kilobat app's network filter is enabled.

tools.name: set_app_rule
tools.description: Saves an allow or block rule for one app, or removes its rule with `reset` so it follows the profile default. Applies to the active travel or work profile, or to `profile` if given; unrestricted has no rules. Identify the app by bundle ID (from get_status `apps[].id`, e.g. com.apple.Music) or process:<name>. Pass `minutes` for a temporary rule. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling. Blocking takes effect only while the Kilobat app's network filter is enabled.

tools.name: set_dns
tools.description: Sets the active network service's DNS to automatic (the network's own resolvers), cloudflare (1.1.1.1), google (8.8.8.8) or quad9 (9.9.9.9), or with `flush` clears the DNS cache, which helps after a site moved or a stale "server not found" but does not make DNS faster. macOS shows the user an administrator password prompt. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling. Suggest restoring automatic if a change does not help.

tools.name: get_wifi
tools.description: The current Wi-Fi link: whether Wi-Fi is on, network name (ssid, null if unavailable), interface, RSSI, noise and signal-to-noise ratio (dB), channel, band, negotiated link rate and a 0–100 signal score. Faster than diagnose_network when only the radio matters. Same JSON as `kilobat wifi status --json`.

tools.name: suggest_wifi_channel
tools.description: Estimates congestion on each candidate channel in the current band from nearby networks and their widths, and names the least crowded one (`recommended`). The user changes the channel in their router's settings; hidden interference can change the best choice. Same JSON as `kilobat channels --json`.

tools.name: get_network_history
tools.description: Records the Kilobat app kept while running. `kind`: `outages` (drops: Unreachable, Wi-Fi roam, Network changed, with start and end), `speed_tests` (earlier speed test results per network) or `health` (periodic router, internet, jitter, loss and DNS measurements). `days` limits the window (1 by default for health, 30 otherwise). A gap means the app was not running, not that nothing happened.

tools.name: benchmark_dns
tools.description: Times lookups of three domains through the system resolver, Cloudflare (1.1.1.1), Google (8.8.8.8) and Quad9 (9.9.9.9). Each entry has `resolver`, `milliseconds` (null if none answered) and `replies` out of 3. Run it twice before recommending a change. Same JSON as `kilobat dns-benchmark`.

tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Requests the headers of one http or https URL and returns the HTTP `status` and cumulative `dnsMs`, `connectMs`, `tlsMs`, `firstByteMs` and `totalMs`, to tell a slow site from a slow connection or DNS. Same JSON as `kilobat http-check <URL> --json`.

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: Open network sockets on this Mac: `pid`, `process`, `transport`, `endpoint` (local -> remote address:port) and `state`. Pass `pid` to narrow to one process, for example one found in get_status `apps[].processIDs`. Same JSON as `kilobat destinations --json`.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Devices this Mac has recently talked to on the local network (the ARP neighbor cache): `address`, `mac`, `interface` and `name`, including names the user gave them in Kilobat. Not a full network scan. Same JSON as `kilobat devices --json`.

tools.name: trace_route
tools.description: A 12-hop route probe to `host`, as plain text. A latency jump that persists to the last hop is real; a single slow hop that recovers is usually a router deprioritizing probes. Each trace is saved. Pass `rounds` (2–5) to trace several times with three probes a hop, like mtr: the text then ends with each hop's loss, best, average, worst and last delay over every saved trace to that host and a line on where the delay starts. Takes up to about 30 seconds a round. Same output as `kilobat trace <host> [--rounds N]`.

tools.name: get_route_history
tools.description: Every saved trace to `host` combined hop by hop, like mtr: `hops` (`ttl`, `addresses` seen there, most often first, `replies` and `probes`, `bestMs`, `averageMs`, `worstMs`, `lastMs`, `changed` when different routers answered in different runs), `runs`, `first` and `last`, `pathChanges` (runs whose routers differ from the run before) and `verdict`, where the delay starts. A hop that skips replies while later hops answer is a router rate-limiting probes, not loss. Without `host`, returns `hosts`, the hosts with saved traces. Same JSON as `kilobat route-history --host <host> --json`.

tools.name: compare_speed_tests
tools.description: Sets two speed tests the Kilobat app saved side by side and lists what was different between them, each with a plain-English note on how it can change a result: `network`, `time` (evening or hours apart), `server` (Cloudflare data center), `method` (one connection or several), `connection` (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, VPN), `vpn`, Wi-Fi `band`, `signal` and `linkRate`, `otherTraffic` on this Mac during the test, idle `latency` and `dataLimit`. Returns `first` and `second` (the earlier test first), `downloadChangePercent`, `uploadChangePercent`, `differences` (`factor`, `first`, `second`, `note`), `unknown` (factors one of the tests didn't record, such as tests saved by an older version) and `summary`. Name tests by `first` and `second`: an id from get_network_history speed_tests, or a place where 1 is the newest; the newest two by default. It lists recorded differences; never claim one of them caused the change, or that a result is wrong. Same JSON as `kilobat speed-compare --json`.

tools.name: get_exit_path
tools.description: Where this Mac's traffic leaves, read on the Mac: the default route's `interface`, `tunnel`, `vpn` (full: the default route goes through a tunnel; partial: a VPN is connected but the default route doesn't use it, so only some destinations go through it; off), `vpnName` (when macOS lists exactly one VPN connected) and `vpnConnected` (every VPN configuration macOS lists as connected). Pass `public_ip` true to also ask Cloudflare which address it sees (`publicIP`) and look up the country it is registered to in Kilobat's local DB-IP data (`publicIPCountry`, `publicIPCountryName`). That sends one request to Cloudflare, so only pass it when the user asks for their public IP or VPN exit. Report it as measured, e.g. "traffic leaves through utun3 (WireGuard), exit IP registered in Germany": the registry country isn't where the user or server is, and neither it nor a VPN shows that a connection is private, anonymous or secure. Same JSON as `kilobat ip [--public] --json`.

tools.name: run_lan_test
tools.description: Five seconds of iperf3 between this Mac and `host`, a device the user runs `iperf3 -s` on, to measure the local network (Wi-Fi, cabling, a mesh link) apart from the internet. `reverse` true has the server send. Returns `receivedMbps`, `sentMbps`, `bytes`, `seconds`, `streams`, `retransmits` (TCP retransmissions on the sending side, when known) and `direction`. Needs iperf3 installed on this Mac by the user; Kilobat never installs it, and the error says how. Moves a lot of data on the local network for five seconds, which can slow other devices meanwhile; it doesn't use the internet unless `host` is on it. Get the user's confirmation first, with the host they named. Same JSON as `kilobat lan-test <host> --json`.

tools.name: list_networks
tools.description: Networks Kilobat has seen, with `key`, `name`, the `profile` and `budgetGB` remembered for each (null if none), data used in the current session there, `current`, the data `cost` the user set (automatic, metered or unmetered) and `metered`, `osMetered` and `meteredSource` (macOS only reports the current network). Same JSON as `kilobat networks --json`.

tools.name: get_conditions
tools.description: Whether now suits a large download or upload or a long unattended run: `connected`, `network` (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, Cellular), `metered` (what Kilobat acts on), `osMetered` (what macOS says) and `meteredSource` (macOS, or you when the user set the network's data cost), `lowDataMode`, `vpn` (the default route goes through a tunnel), `vpnInterface`, `vpnName` and `vpnConnected` (VPNs macOS lists as connected, which may carry only some destinations; get_exit_path has the detail), `internetLatencyMs` and `internetLossPercent` from a quick ping, `power` (`batteryPercent`, `onAC`, `thermal`, `lowPowerMode`), whether Kilobat keeps the Mac awake (`keptAwake`, `awakeReasons`, `awakeUntil` for keep_awake), `awakeOnPower` (`enabled`, `display`, `active`: the user's own Stay awake while plugged in setting, which no tool changes), `updaters` (`pauseOnMetered`, the setting, and `paused`, whether the filter pauses updaters on this network now; get_updaters has the detail) and one line of `advice`. Takes about 2 seconds. Same JSON as `kilobat conditions --json`.

tools.name: get_updaters
tools.description: Whether Kilobat pauses updater helpers on metered networks (`enabled`, on unless the user turned it off), whether this network is `metered` and they are `paused` now, and `filterActive` (null when the Kilobat app isn't running; pausing needs its network filter). `covered` lists the helpers it recognizes (`downloads` is false for Sparkle's and Squirrel's installers, which only install what the app already downloaded). `gotThrough` lists update bytes on the current network: an updater's own, or a System downloads service such as nsurlsessiond that connected for one (`shared`, so its bytes include other downloads); null without the running app. `pausedConnections` counts updater connections the filter stopped in the last 24 hours. `inProcess` lists installed apps that update from inside their own process (Sparkle or Squirrel), which can't be paused without blocking the app. `limits` says what pausing can't do. Same JSON as `kilobat updaters --json`.

tools.name: diagnose_connection
tools.description: Checks why one website, API or host can't be reached from this Mac, layer by layer: the Mac's network and the interface it uses (Wi-Fi, Ethernet, a phone hotspot or a VPN), the system proxy and PAC file, DNS and its resolver (including a VPN's private resolver for its domain), Kilobat's own rules, TCP and TLS over IPv4 and IPv6 separately, the same connection over each interface when there are several, the exact request (path and query kept) through the path the app uses, every redirect hop with its own IPv4 and IPv6 check of the final host, and with a VPN or proxy on, the direct path against the tunnel or proxy. A HEAD request the server refuses is retried once as a one-byte GET; nothing larger is downloaded. A broken IPv6 or IPv4 path, a tunnel that fails while direct connections work, a proxy that works where direct connections are blocked, and a redirect target that fails each get their own verdict. A passing check means this request from this Mac over that path works now, not that every app or transfer is fine. Returns `verdict`, `next` (what to do), `ok`, `steps` (`layer`, `status`: ok, warning, failed or skipped, and `detail`), `hops` (`url`, `host`, `method`, `status` or `error`), `method` (what the check sent: HEAD, or a one-byte GET), `path` (`kind`: appProxy, environmentProxy, systemProxy or direct; `proxy` as host:port; `untested`, an app setting the check couldn't go through), `client` (`id`, `name`, `version` of the app as installed), `date` (when the check ran) and `failedAt`. `target`, details and hop URLs never show query values or passwords. Pass `app` (a bundle ID or process:<name> from get_status) to include that app's rules, the proxy variables in its environment (HTTPS_PROXY, ALL_PROXY, NO_PROXY) and its open connections to the host or its proxy, compared with the fresh one, and a `Transfer` step that says whether bytes still arrive on them a few seconds apart. A quiet transfer may be stalled or finished with its connection still open: never report a download as finished from it. Pass `proxy` when the app uses a proxy address from its own settings: the request goes through it, and when that fails while direct connections work, the verdict says the network is fine and the app's path isn't. Some apps have a setting Kilobat can't read or go through, such as LM Studio's Hugging Face proxy (a switch with no address) for huggingface.co downloads: an `App setting` step cites dated user reports, and the verdict says the network works, not that the app's request does. Suggest the user checks that setting; never change another app's settings or promise it will resume a download on its own. Pass `failed_at` when the user says when the app failed. Pass `context` when the failing code runs in a container, VM or remote machine: the checks still run on this Mac, and a `Context` step says how to check from there. Pass `context` provider when a hosted service makes the request from its own servers (Warp's custom inference endpoint, say; pass its `app`, dev.warp.Warp-Stable, to name it): a `Provider` step says whether the target is private (localhost, a LAN or Tailscale address, a name only private DNS knows), which those servers can't reach however well it works from the Mac. Picking a known provider as `app` adds that step on its own, worded as an if. Never suggest SSH into the provider or exposing the Mac's service through a tunnel; the options are a public endpoint the user controls or a route the provider supports, quoted from `next`. When the user describes a slow or failing transfer already under way, say that a fresh check can't see that connection, and suggest get_app_bandwidth for it. Takes up to about 30 seconds. Same JSON as `kilobat why <target> --json`.

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Awake sessions and AI agent runs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) the Kilobat app recorded over the last `days` (7 by default), newest first: `kind` (awake or agent), `title`, `start`, `end`, `ended` (Finished, Failed, Went quiet, Exited, Timer ended, Turned off); for agent runs the agent's hooks report, `session`, `cwd`, `project` and `state` (working, waitingForYou, done, stalled, networkFailed or failed; the last one seen for an ended run), `note` (e.g. Rate-limited until 3pm), `lastEvent` (last hook), `lastActive` (last traffic) and `lastCPU` (last CPU work), and `sharedTraffic` when bytes may include other runs of the same agent; only `ended` Finished means the agent said it was done. `executable`, `origin` (Homebrew, npm (node 22.3.0), Claude app…), `version` and `otherInstalls` show which install ran; bytes `received` and `sent`, bytes per process (`apps`), `destinations` an agent contacted, `events` (network changes during the run), `batteryStart`, `batteryEnd` and `peakThermal`. Recorded only while the app runs. Same JSON as `kilobat sessions --json --days N`.

tools.name: keep_awake
tools.description: Stops this Mac from idle-sleeping for `minutes` (1–240) so a long build, download or agent run isn't cut off. Calling again replaces the previous hold; it ends early with release_awake or when this MCP server stops. Shows in `pmset -g assertions` as "Kilobat: <reason>". Changes no settings and is low risk: tell the user for how long, and on battery get their confirmation first. Closing the lid still sleeps the Mac unless `lid_closed` is true: then the Kilobat app's power helper keeps it running with the lid shut, which works only after the user allowed it in Kilobat Settings and approved the helper. A closed Mac in a bag can overheat and drains its battery, so get the user's explicit confirmation for lid_closed every time, saying for how long; Kilobat still lets it sleep at the user's battery floor, when it runs hot, and when the time is up. `lidHold` in the result says until when, and `lidFloor` at which battery percentage it gives up.

tools.name: release_awake
tools.description: Ends a keep_awake hold early, with its lid-closed hold if any, so the Mac can sleep again. `released` is false when there was none. Releasing needs no confirmation.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Sets the current network's data budget: `gb` (0.1–10000), when it starts over (`cycle`: session only resets by hand, or daily, weekly, monthly), `reset_day` (1–31 for monthly, 1 Monday to 7 Sunday for weekly) and `alerts`, the percentages that notify once per cycle ("50,80,100" or "none"). Omitted values stay as they are. With the Kilobat app's filter on, new connections stop once it is used up in the travel and work profiles; unrestricted only tracks it. Usage is sampled, so the cap is approximate. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling.

tools.name: set_network_cost
tools.description: Sets what the current network, or `network` (a key or name from list_networks), costs. `metered` gets the protection of a phone hotspot: Kilobat switches to Travel (when that is on and no profile is remembered for the network) and skips scheduled speed tests. Use it for Android hotspots and USB or Ethernet tethering that macOS doesn't flag. `unmetered` overrides macOS, `automatic` follows it again. Kilobat refuses a network it can't tell apart, such as Wi-Fi whose name macOS hides without Location access. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling.

tools.name: set_updater_pause
tools.description: Turns pausing updaters on metered networks `on` (the default) or `off`. While on and the network is metered, the Kilobat app's network filter blocks updater helpers (Google Updater, Microsoft AutoUpdate, macOS Software Update, App Store downloads, Sparkle's and Squirrel's helpers) with an ordinary rule; the apps themselves keep working, nothing in other apps or macOS changes, and updates resume on an unmetered network. Returns `enabled`, `metered`, `paused` and the `effect` in words. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling.

tools.name: set_app_quota
tools.description: Limits how much data one app may use per budget cycle (daily with a session budget), counting `direction` total or upload only, on this `network` or on all of them. With the Kilobat app's filter on, its new connections stop once the quota is used up, as with the budget; a temporary allow rule still lets it through. `action` remove deletes the app's quotas. Identify the app by bundle ID (get_status `apps[].id`) or process:<name>. Usage is sampled, so it is approximate. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling.

tools.name: get_app_bandwidth
tools.description: Bytes one app sent and received in a calendar `range` (hour, day, week or month), split into buckets (minutes, hours, six-hour blocks or days), with totals and the peak rate and when it happened. Omit `app` for all traffic. `back` steps to earlier periods: 1 is the previous hour, day, week or month. Use the app names from get_usage_report `topApps` or get_status `apps[].name`; helpers count under the app that owns them. History is recorded while the Kilobat app runs. Same JSON as `kilobat bandwidth [app] <range> --back N --json`.

tools.name: get_access_policy
tools.description: What an app's developer says it connects to and why, from the Internet Access Policy file some apps ship (CleanShot X, Raycast, 1Password and others): `description`, `developer`, and `connections` with `hosts`, `port`, `purpose`, `denyConsequences` and whether each is `essential`. `declared` is false when the app ships none. Use it before blocking a domain an app needs. Same JSON as `kilobat access-policy <bundle-id> --json`.

tools.name: set_new_app_mode
tools.description: What Travel and Work do with apps that have no rule: `allow` lets them connect, `ask` holds their first connections until the user allows or blocks them in the Kilobat app (or you do with decide_approval), `block` blocks them silently. `allow_apple` lets Apple's own software through when asking or blocking. Unrestricted always allows. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling. Takes effect only while the Kilobat app's network filter is enabled.

tools.name: list_approvals
tools.description: Apps the Kilobat filter is holding while new apps are asked about: `app` (rule key), `process`, `path`, `signer` and `signatureValid`, `pid`, `requests`, how many connections are `waiting`, and `destinations` (`host`, `address`, `port`). Held connections give up after a minute. Needs the Kilobat app running. Same JSON as `kilobat approvals --json`.

tools.name: decide_approval
tools.description: Answers an approval from list_approvals. `block` drops its held connections and saves a block rule in the active profile at once; pass `minutes` to block for a while only. `allow` doesn't apply by itself: it opens Kilobat's approval window on that app so the person confirms it, and returns `confirming: true`. Check the signature and destinations first. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling.

tools.name: block_destination
tools.description: Blocks or unblocks a `target` domain (subdomains included; *.example.com is accepted), IP address or CIDR range for every app, or with `app` for that app only as a connection rule in the active profile. Check get_access_policy first so you don't cut off a connection an app needs. Changes the user's settings: explain what will change and get explicit confirmation before calling. Takes effect on new connections while the Kilobat app's network filter is enabled.

tools.name: list_blocked_connections
tools.description: Connections the Kilobat filter blocked in the last `days` (1 by default, up to 7), newest first: `date`, `app`, `endpoint`, `direction` and `reason` (app rule, blocklist entry, connection rule, budget, default deny or a block when asked). Metadata only. Same data as `kilobat blocked-history`.

tools.name: run_stutter_test
tools.description: Pings the router (or `target`: internet for 1.1.1.1, or a host) every 50 ms for `seconds` (20 by default) to find the short latency spikes that make calls, game streaming and remote desktops stutter while speed and loss look fine. Returns `latencyMs` (p50, p95, p99, max), `lossPercent` (`pingRateLimited` is true when the router answers only some fast pings, which is not real loss), `spikes` (`atSeconds`, `peakMs`; a spike is over 3× the median and over 50 ms), `periodSeconds` when spikes repeat at a regular interval, `pattern` (steady, few, periodic, irregular, noReplies), `awdl` (the AirDrop link and what used it) and a plain `verdict`. Regular spikes on the router often come from AirDrop/AWDL scanning, but not always; a speed test can't see them. Sends pings only. Same JSON as `kilobat stutter --json` without the raw samples.

tools.name: get_nearby_radios
tools.description: The radios that share this Mac's Wi-Fi chip or band: `awdl` (whether the AirDrop link is up and active and which features use it: AirDrop, Universal Control, Sidecar, iPhone Mirroring, Continuity), AirDrop `visibility` (everyone, contacts, off), Bluetooth `devices` (`name`, `kind`, `connected`, `sharesBand`), the Wi-Fi band and coexistence `advice` when Bluetooth audio or input devices share 2.4 GHz with Wi-Fi.

tools.name: set_airdrop_visibility
tools.description: Asks for AirDrop visibility `everyone`, `contacts` or `off`. macOS lets only System Settings change it, so this opens System Settings at General › AirDrop & Handoff for the user to choose, and returns the current `visibility` and `openedSettings`. Opens a window on the user's screen: explain why and get the user's explicit confirmation before calling.
